facts.text: On this date in 1859, the first practical elevator with a safety brake was installed in a New York building — not for passengers, but for freight. Human elevator travel was still considered too dangerous.
Manila is the world's most densely populated city proper, packing over 70,000 people per square kilometer — denser than any neighborhood in New York or Tokyo.
On this date in 1927, the Holland Tunnel opened as the first mechanically ventilated underwater vehicle tunnel. Engineers had genuinely feared car exhaust would kill drivers within minutes.
More people live inside a 4,000km radius centered on Bangladesh than outside it — over half of all humanity fits in that single circle.
Canada is larger than the entire European Union by land area, yet has fewer people than the state of California.

On this day in 1929, two weeks after Black Tuesday, the Dow fell another 6% — markets were still unraveling. The full bottom wouldn't arrive for nearly three more years, with the index down 89% from its peak.
On Nov 12, 1974, the SEC approved negotiated commissions, ending a 180-year-old system of fixed brokerage fees. Discount brokers like Schwab were born within months.
The New York Stock Exchange traces its founding to 24 brokers signing the Buttonwood Agreement under a tree on Wall Street — the annual membership fee was $25.
Saudi Aramco's 2019 IPO raised $25.6 billion, the largest in history. It briefly made the company worth $2 trillion — more than Apple, Google, and Amazon combined at the time.
The entire country of Zimbabwe once issued a 100 trillion dollar banknote. It was worth about 40 US cents on the day it was printed.

On this date in 1980, Voyager 1 made its closest approach to Saturn, revealing that the planet's rings are only about 10 meters thick despite spanning 282,000 kilometers — thinner, proportionally, than a sheet of paper.
On this date in 1833, the Leonid meteor storm rained roughly 100,000 shooting stars per hour over North America, convincing many observers the sky itself was falling.
Your body contains about 37 trillion cells, yet you are outnumbered 10 to 1 by the microbial cells living on and inside you — most of human biology is not genetically human.

A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city, making its surface gravity 200 billion times stronger than Earth's — a marshmallow dropped from one meter would hit it with the energy of an atomic bomb.

Tardigrades can survive the vacuum of open space, temperatures near absolute zero, and radiation doses 1,000 times lethal to humans — they achieve this by replacing their cellular water with a glass-like sugar that suspends life entirely.
On this day in 1980, Voyager 1 made its closest approach to Saturn — the same year CNN launched and Mount St. Helens erupted. The spacecraft is now in interstellar space, still transmitting.
Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire. Teaching began at Oxford around 1096; the Aztecs founded Tenochtitlán in 1325.
On this day in 1942, the Naval Battle of Guadalcanal began — a turning point so decisive that Japan never again mounted a major offensive in the Pacific.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She died in 30 BC; the pyramid was finished around 2560 BC.
The fax machine was invented in 1843 — before the American Civil War, before the telephone, and 140 years before most offices actually got one.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Coined by John Koenig in *The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows*, it feels ancient because it was built to.
Sonder (n.): the realization that every passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Another Koenig coinage, now common enough that people argue it deserves a dictionary entry.
On this day in 1936, the Oxford English Dictionary completed its first edition — a 12-volume, 414,825-entry project begun in 1857. It took 70 years longer than originally promised.
Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word from Tierra del Fuego meaning the look shared by two people who both want something neither will initiate. Yaghan is nearly extinct; this word outlives its language.
On this day in 1980, Voyager 1 made its closest approach to Saturn — and English gained a problem: no word existed for the awe of seeing a planet as a real place. 'Sublime' had to do.

On this date in 2021, Ethereum's EIP-3529 had been live for months — it permanently reduced gas refunds, cutting a loophole that let bots profit by filling storage slots purely to claim refunds later.

On Nov 12, 2017, Bitcoin Cash forked again into Bitcoin Gold, giving the month two BCH-family splits — a sign that "fork as governance" had become the dominant conflict-resolution mechanism of that era.

Satoshi's genesis block coinbase contains the text 'The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — not just a timestamp, but an unforgeable proof that no coins were premined before that date.

The Bitcoin script opcode OP_RETURN was originally disabled by Satoshi for security reasons, reintroduced in 0.9.0 capped at 40 bytes, then expanded to 80 — each change reflects a decade-long war over what a blockchain is actually for.

Ethereum's uncle rate — orphaned blocks included for partial reward — peaked near 25% during 2016 congestion, revealing that at high throughput, proof-of-work networks structurally favor miners with the lowest-latency connections to peers.

On this date in 2016, Google DeepMind's AlphaGo paper appeared in Nature — the first system to defeat a professional Go player without handicap, using 1,920 CPUs and 280 GPUs to simulate games against itself.
On this date in 2021, the Machine Learning Reproducibility Checklist became mandatory at NeurIPS, an admission that the field had spent a decade publishing results that often couldn't be replicated.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average US homes, spent on a single model.

The transformer architecture, now the foundation of virtually every frontier AI system, was introduced in a 2017 paper whose authors have since scattered across at least six different companies and labs.

Reinforcement learning from human feedback uses surprisingly few labeled comparisons — OpenAI's InstructGPT alignment was achieved with under 40,000 human preference judgments layered onto a model trained on hundreds of billions of tokens.
